**Finding 1. "United States Census, 1900" — indexing error (birth year)**

Citation: "United States Census, 1900", database with images, FamilySearch, entry for Christian P. Hole, Fairview Township, Polk County, Minnesota, ED 112, sheet 4B.

The indexed record gives his birth year as **1877**. The profile records **1875**, which is also confirmed by the Minnesota Death Index (Finding 2 below), which draws from civil-registration stock and gives 1875.

Everything else in the 1900 census entry is consistent with this person: the name Christian P. Hole, the correct household in Fairview Township, Polk County, wife Inger, and son Ole C. The birth year alone is the point of difference. A two-year variance between a census age and a civil-registration record is the kind of drift that arises when ages are estimated or reported by whoever answered the door, but the death index is an exact record and the gap is two full years — enough to treat it as a transcription error rather than ordinary census drift.

This collection is described as "database with images", so the original page is available.

Recommended action: Open the original census page in FamilySearch and verify what year is actually written in the birth column. If the page reads 1877, investigate whether the household member was mis-identified at indexing; if the handwriting is consistent with 1875, submit a correction to the index entry. Keep the source attached either way — it is strong evidence for the 1900 residence and household, with one suspect field.

---

**Finding 2. "Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002" — indexing error (death year)**

Citation: "Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002", database, FamilySearch, entry for Christian P. Hole, died 10 June 1945, Polk County, Minnesota.

The indexed record gives the death date as **10 June 1954**. The profile records **10 June 1945**. The name, county and day-and-month are identical; the year is out by exactly nine years. The month and day matching precisely, with only the year different, is characteristic of a transcription error in a handwritten or typed register entry where the final digit of the year was misread or keyed incorrectly.

This collection is described as "database" only — no images. There is no page to open in FamilySearch. The underlying source is the Minnesota death certificate or the state death register from which this index was compiled.

Recommended action: Obtain the original death certificate for Christian P. Hole from the Minnesota Department of Health or the Polk County vital records office to confirm the year. If the certificate reads 1945, use FamilySearch's index-correction pathway on this entry to report the error. Keep the source attached; the correct death date is already on the profile from another record and this index is still evidence of the death event.

---

**Finding 3. "Minnesota State Census, 1885" — misattributed source**

Citation: "Minnesota State Census, 1885", database, FamilySearch, entry for Christian Hole, Otter Tail County, Minnesota.

This record does not fit Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2). The indexed subject was born in **1852** and was living in **Aurdal, Otter Tail County** in 1885 with a wife named Bergit and a son Nils (born 1879 in Minnesota). Christian P. Hole's profile gives a birth year of **1875** — which means the 1885 census subject was already a grown man with a wife and child when Christian P. Hole was approximately ten years old and, on the profile evidence, still in Norway. The county is also different: this person's life is in Otter Tail County, while Christian P. Hole's documented Minnesota life is in Polk County.

The source is also attached to KD96-WX7, a separate tree person named Christian Hole. I read that profile: it gives birth year **1852**, a 1885 residence in **Aurdal, Otter Tail, Minnesota**, and a death in **1919 in Aurdal, Otter Tail**. Every field in the 1885 census record — year of birth, county, township — aligns with KD96-WX7. That is a different individual, a generation older, in a different county.

Recommended action: Detach this record from Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2). The indexed subject's birth year (1852), household composition (wife Bergit, son Nils) and county (Otter Tail) are incompatible with this person's profile at multiple independent points. The record's own details fit KD96-WX7 consistently.

---

**Sources that could not be checked**

The fourth attached source — "Hole family photograph and funeral card (uploaded memory)" — is a contributor-uploaded document with no indexed record behind it. There is no readable record ARK, so its contents cannot be verified through the tools available here. Its citation describes it as a funeral card for Christian P. Hole, Erskine, Minnesota, 1945, which is consistent with the profile, but the claim rests on the contributor's upload and not on anything this audit can confirm. If the card's text matters for a specific fact (the exact death date, burial place, survivors), a researcher with access to the image should read it directly.

---

**From FamilySearch's own profile checklist — suggestions for the profile, not errors in a source, and not counted above:**

VERIFIABILITY
- The marriage has no tagged sources.

COMPLETENESS
- A marriage place is missing a city.

---

In summary: three user-actionable findings — a birth-year indexing error in the 1900 census, a death-year indexing error in the death index, and a clearly misattributed 1885 Minnesota census entry that belongs to an older same-surname man in a different county. FamilySearch's quality check flagged no source conflicts of its own; the two profile issues it raised concern the marriage fact, which has no attached source at all and so fell outside this audit's scope.
